project.name: mold-frontend-workspace
project.description: Mold is a CLI-native local AI image and video generation system that runs on NVIDIA CUDA and Apple GPUs and exposes REST and SSE interfaces for local and remote workflows. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

layers.name: Core Platform
layers.description: Rust crates implementing Mold’s inference engines, shared core contracts, SQLite persistence, HTTP server, CLI, Discord, catalog, and TUI runtime.

layers.name: Desktop Application
layers.description: The Tauri desktop application, including its Vue workspaces, native bridge, packaging integration, and desktop-specific tests.

layers.name: Shared Studio
layers.description: Shared Studio UI contracts, generation workflows, gallery behavior, routing, and reusable client logic consumed by Mold surfaces.

layers.name: Web Client
layers.description: The browser-facing Vue/Vite application that presents Mold Studio through the shared Studio contract.

layers.name: Mobile Application
layers.description: The remote-only iOS and Android Tauri application, native mobile bridges, generated platform projects, and mobile release assets.

layers.name: Design System
layers.description: Shared Mold Studio visual primitives, theme tokens, icons, styles, and reusable Vue presentation components.

layers.name: Project Support
layers.description: Root-level tooling, developer scripts, Nix and packaging helpers, tests, contributor utilities, and analysis support files.

layers.name: Configuration
layers.description: Build manifests, workspace settings, Tauri metadata, formatter and tool configuration, and other project configuration records.

layers.name: Delivery Automation
layers.description: GitHub Actions pipelines and infrastructure service definitions that build, test, package, sign, and publish Mold releases.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Maintainer and user documentation, changelog fragments, website content, and architecture or release guidance for Mold.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to frame Mold as a local AI image and video generation system rather than a single executable. It provides the vocabulary for the Rust engine, HTTP server, and the desktop, web, and mobile clients that the following stops connect into one architecture.

tour.title: Workspace Foundations
tour.description: Cargo.toml is the configuration anchor for the Rust workspace and its feature-gated crates. Read it after the overview to see how shared contracts, persistence, inference, server, CLI, and supporting runtimes are assembled into buildable units.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo manifests declare packages, workspace membership, dependencies, and feature flags declaratively; feature gating lets Mold keep platform-specific GPU and media paths out of builds that do not need them.

tour.title: CLI Runtime Entry
tour.description: The mold-cli main.rs file is the first executable stop: it turns the workspace foundation into the command-line runtime users invoke. It is a useful map of how commands such as generation, serving, model management, and queue inspection enter the shared platform.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's main function typically composes parsed values and fallible initialization with Result-returning operations, making error propagation explicit at the application boundary.

tour.title: Shared Core Contracts
tour.description: Build on the CLI by reading mold-core's types.rs and client.rs, which define the vocabulary and HTTP-facing client behavior shared across local and remote execution. These high-fan-in files are the contract boundary: later server and UI layers can coordinate because they exchange the same typed requests, status, model, and media concepts.

tour.title: HTTP API Boundary
tour.description: The server routes.rs module exposes the core capabilities to every client, while execution_plan.rs turns an accepted generation request into concrete work. Together they show the boundary between validation and admission on one side and the engine-facing plan on the other, including the point where local and remote hosts share one wire contract.

tour.title: Queue And Scheduling
tour.description: Once a request becomes an execution plan, scheduler/mod.rs coordinates admission and work ordering, while queue_journal.rs records durable queue state. This explains why Mold can report progress, recover queued work, and keep multiple generation targets coherent instead of treating each request as an isolated function call.
tour.languageLesson: Rust modules commonly encapsulate stateful coordination behind structs and traits; ownership and borrowing make queue mutation explicit while keeping concurrent workers from aliasing mutable state unsafely.

tour.title: Persistence And Recovery
tour.description: mold-db's db.rs is the persistence anchor behind gallery records, settings, history, and recovery metadata. Read it after scheduling to connect durable queue behavior and generated artifacts to SQLite-backed state that survives process restarts and supports the clients' library views.

tour.title: Inference Runtime
tour.description: The inference engine.rs and device.rs modules translate an admitted plan into model execution on the selected backend, while ltx2/runtime.rs illustrates how a substantial model family plugs into that runtime. This is the computational core: it owns device-aware execution and progress-producing model work without requiring the UI to know model internals.

tour.title: Shared Studio Layer
tour.description: The shared studio entry point and its hostRouting.ts and chainTypes.ts modules carry the cross-surface generation vocabulary into TypeScript. They centralize host selection, multi-step sequence contracts, and reusable client logic so desktop, web, and mobile can present different shells while preserving the same request and routing semantics.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript modules can act as a shared contract layer: explicit types and discriminated request shapes let several Vue clients share behavior while still narrowing safely for one-shot versus sequence output.

tour.title: Client Surface Bootstraps
tour.description: The desktop main.ts, web main.ts and App.vue, and mobile main.ts and MobileApp.vue files show how the same Studio concepts become three user-facing products. Desktop can pair a native Tauri shell with a local engine, web presents the browser client, and mobile remains a remote-only surface with its own native bridge while reusing shared contracts.

tour.title: Container Packaging
tour.description: The root Dockerfile describes how Mold is packaged for a deployable environment after the runtime layers are understood. Its build stages connect the Rust/server artifact and web assets to a repeatable image, making the same API boundary available outside a developer workstation.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate compilation dependencies from the smaller runtime image; ordering stable dependency steps before frequently changing source steps also improves layer-cache reuse.

tour.title: Continuous Delivery
tour.description: Finish with ci.yml and release.yml to see how Mold validates the cross-layer contract and turns passing builds into shipped artifacts. These pipelines are the architectural capstone: they enforce Rust, client, mobile, packaging, and release checks so changes remain coherent across the surfaces introduced in the tour.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows model triggers, jobs, and steps; independent jobs can validate platform-specific targets in parallel, while release jobs compose only after required checks succeed.
